COMPLETE VISIBLE RESPONSE (math reproduced from visible TeX annotations; citations retain visible URLs):

I have not resolved the unrestricted deterministic FPTAS question. I have neither constructed the required uniform algorithm nor proved an impossibility result for it. The supplied advances do not close that gap, and the additional constructions below do not justify declaring it closed.

The strongest completed results from this turn are:

- A self-contained, polynomial-bit equivalence between the requested permanent FPTAS and a deterministic FPTAS for the weighted bipartite all-matchings partition function. Both directions have explicit positive constructions, rational enclosures and charged weight sizes.

- An exact family showing that every matching coefficient below the permanent can agree while the permanents differ by a factor of two, together with a quantitative limitation on bounded-fugacity scalar observations.

- A rational-height obstruction to hiding a superpolynomial exact amplification power inside a polynomial-size explicitly encoded rational matrix.

- A complete conditional FPTAS under an explicitly specified logarithmic-seed pseudorandom-generator hypothesis. The hypothesis remains additional and unproved here.

These results preserve concrete mathematical information about the attempted routes. None is a general lower bound for the input model in your question.

1. What the current premises establish

I read Kudria–Luo–Majid’s Theorems 1.1–1.2, Section 2 and Appendices A–D, together with the relevant evaluator and optimization arguments. Their governing tradeoff is

$$\log(U/L)\le \frac{2n}{\sqrt{e\lambda}}+8\eta n,$$

with bit work

$$\operatorname{poly}\!\left(
B+n+\operatorname{bits}\lambda+\operatorname{bits}\eta,
\lambda,\eta^{-1}
\right)
\exp\!\left(
O\!\left(\sqrt{\lambda}\log^2\frac{\lambda}{\eta}\right)
\right).$$

The normalization, optimization and rational rounding are paid. Setting $\lambda=\Theta((n/\epsilon)^2)$ and $\eta=\Theta(\epsilon/n)$ obtains relative accuracy, but this bound does not become polynomial. Their fixed-power-saving amplification remains available; their present logarithmic saving does not meet its hypothesis. arxiv.org [https://arxiv.org/html/2609.10516v1?utm_source=chatgpt.com]

Final response

The direct reduction is valid, including its complete bit costs.

Let $P=\operatorname{per}(A)>0$, and write $Z(A)=\sum_{k=0}^n m_k(A)$. For complete input bit length $B_A$,

$$P\ge 2^{-B_A},
\qquad
Z(A)\le 2^{B_A}(n+1)^n.$$

The first bound follows from any positive perfect-matching term. For the second, every matching has weight at most $2^{B_A}$, and a matching can be encoded by one choice in $\{0,\ldots,n\}$ for each row, giving at most $(n+1)^n$ matchings. Thus

$$Q=2^{2B_A}(n+1)^n$$

bounds $Z(A)/P$.

Set $t=\lceil 8Q/\epsilon\rceil$. Since $t\ge1$,

$$t^{-n}Z(tA)
=
P+\sum_{k<n}m_k(A)t^{k-n}
\le P+\frac{Z(A)}t
\le(1+\epsilon/8)P.$$

Therefore, from a certified interval $L_Z\le Z(tA)\le U_Z$ of ratio $1+\epsilon/4$, the endpoints

$$L=\frac{L_Z}{t^n(1+\epsilon/8)},
\qquad
U=\frac{U_Z}{t^n}$$

satisfy

$$L\le P\le U,\qquad
\frac UL\le(1+\epsilon/4)(1+\epsilon/8)\le1+\epsilon.$$

All construction costs are polynomial:

$$\operatorname{bits}(t)
=
O\!\left(B_A+n\log(n+1)+\operatorname{bits}(\epsilon)\right),$$

$$\operatorname{bits}(tA)
\le B_A+O(n^2\operatorname{bits}(t)),
\qquad
\operatorname{bits}(t^n)=O(n\operatorname{bits}(t)).$$

Exact support matching handles $P=0$; $n=0$, if allowed, is immediate.

Combined with the positive reservoir construction in the earlier report, this proves the self-contained full rational-bit equivalence between a deterministic permanent FPTAS and a deterministic weighted bipartite all-matchings FPTAS.

The KLM optimizer remains useful for its stronger reduction: it only needs a partition evaluator at a numerically polynomial weight budget. This direct reduction uses weights whose bit lengths are polynomial but whose numerical size can be exponential.
